priorStories.headline: Democrats win control of the U.S. House
priorStories.body:
The Associated Press called the House for Democrats early Wednesday after the party won more than the 218 seats required for control.

Combined with their Senate victory, the result gives Democrats both chambers when the new Congress convenes in January, ending two years of unified Republican control. The final size of the House majority remained unsettled.

priorStories.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison
priorStories.body:
A Hong Kong court sentenced pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to 10 years in prison after he pleaded guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces under the national security law imposed by Beijing.

Wong was already serving four years and eight months in a separate national security case. The remaining two months of that term will run concurrently with the new sentence.

priorStories.headline: Senate elections produce several historic firsts
priorStories.body:
Michigan elected Democrat Abdul El-Sayed as the first Muslim U.S. senator. Minnesota’s Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the Senate, while New Hampshire’s Chris Pappas became its first openly gay male member.

Illinois also elected Julia Stratton, meaning three Black women will serve in the Senate simultaneously for the first time.

candidates.summary: Indiana executed Jeffrey Weisheit by lethal injection at 12:45 a.m. Eastern time. Weisheit, 50, had been sentenced to death for killing his girlfriend’s two children in a 2010 house fire. His execution was the first of three scheduled in the United States on Thursday.
candidates.title: Indiana executes Jeffrey Weisheit

candidates.summary: Bomb threats disrupted several European flights Thursday morning. An Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome carrying 151 people was escorted to a French military base, while Italian military jets escorted a Finnair flight from Helsinki to Rome. Authorities found nothing unusual aboard the Finnair aircraft; no responsibility for the threats was immediately reported.
candidates.title: Bomb threats disrupt multiple European flights

candidates.summary: French trade unions launched nationwide strikes and demonstrations seeking higher wages and supporting an ongoing high-school protest movement. The action added to pressure on President Emmanuel Macron’s government after weeks of civil unrest and student protests.
candidates.title: French unions begin nationwide strike action

candidates.summary: A three-alarm fire tore through a two-story row house in Brooklyn’s Sunset Park neighborhood early Thursday, killing six people and injuring nine, including three firefighters and two police officers. More than 200 first responders attended, and four residents were rescued. Fire marshals were investigating the cause; officials said a lithium-ion battery was found but had not been linked to the fire.
candidates.title: Six killed in Brooklyn house fire

candidates.summary: The British government said a British man being treated for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was being medically evacuated to the United Kingdom. The patient, believed to be a healthcare worker, was expected to enter a high-level isolation unit at London’s Royal Free Hospital. British authorities assessed the risk to the public as low.
candidates.title: British Ebola patient evacuated from Congo
candidates.geography: Democratic Republic of the Congo and United Kingdom

candidates.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged large overnight drone attacks. Ukraine said it intercepted or suppressed 105 of 128 Russian drones, with strikes wounding four people in the Kyiv and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Russia said it shot down 496 Ukrainian drones; a Russian regional governor reported one person wounded in Ryazan. Moscow-installed officials in occupied Luhansk said a Ukrainian strike on a bus killed five people and wounded 13; the claims were not independently verified.
candidates.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange large drone attacks

candidates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the confirmed death toll from Monday’s Russian guided-bomb strike on a former school and nearby aid shelter in Komyshuvakha had risen to 43. Rescuers continued searching for more than 30 people believed trapped in the wreckage, while one previously missing person was found alive.
candidates.title: Death toll from Ukraine aid-site strike rises to 43

candidates.summary: The European Commission transferred €4.36 billion to Ukraine from a €90 billion loan agreed by European Union leaders in April. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the tranche would support defense and essential public services; Zelenskyy said it would help fund energy resilience, drones, electronic warfare and air defenses.
candidates.title: European Commission transfers €4.36 billion to Ukraine

candidates.summary: Authorities said more than a dozen European flights received bomb threats Thursday, prompting emergency landings, searches and military escorts. No hazardous or suspicious materials were found, and a British official described the threats as malicious hoaxes. Investigators had not established whether the incidents were connected or identified who was responsible.
candidates.title: More than a dozen European flights receive bomb threats

candidates.summary: The S&P 500 closed down 4.4%, its largest one-day decline since April 2025, as a sell-off led by companies associated with artificial-intelligence data centers erased the previous day’s gains. The Dow fell 1,833 points, or 3.4%, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq dropped 5.5%, entering correction territory relative to its October high.
candidates.title: AI-led sell-off sends major U.S. stock indexes sharply lower

candidates.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced his resignation amid a crisis caused by the collapse of Ueno Bank, which left millions of customers unable to access accounts. The lower house voted 78-0 to send impeachment charges to the Senate and rejected an impeachment effort against Vice President Pedro Alliana. A later congressional session considering Peña’s resignation ended without a decision after losing its quorum, leaving the transfer of power unresolved at the observation cutoff.
candidates.title: Paraguay president resigns as lawmakers advance impeachment

candidates.summary: Court documents unsealed Thursday showed that the Trump administration held talks with Iran about deporting Iranian nationals while the countries were at war. The documents said the administration had discussed sending detainees through an unnamed third country but did not identify a finalized plan. A federal judge ordered the government to provide advance notice before carrying out such deportations.
candidates.title: Court documents reveal U.S.-Iran deportation talks

candidates.summary: Florida, Alabama and Indiana carried out lethal-injection executions Thursday. Jesse Guardado was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. in Florida for the 2004 murder of Jackie Malone, while Michael Taylor was pronounced dead at 6:10 p.m. Central time in Alabama for killing Ivan and Lucille Moore in 1991. Indiana had executed Jeffrey Weisheit shortly after midnight for killing two children in a 2010 house fire. Florida’s 19th execution of 2026 tied its annual record.
candidates.title: Three U.S. states carry out executions on the same day
candidates.geography: Indiana, Florida and Alabama, United States

candidates.summary: A federal judge issued a temporary restraining order preventing the Trump administration from beginning construction of a proposed 250-foot memorial arch for 14 days. The ruling came shortly after the National Capital Planning Commission approved the project 8-4. Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered a government compliance report for Monday; the order did not resolve the underlying dispute over whether the project requires congressional approval.
candidates.title: Judge temporarily blocks construction of Trump’s memorial arch
candidates.geography: Washington, D.C., and Virginia, United States

candidates.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña remained formally in office after Congress did not accept his offered resignation. The Chamber of Deputies voted 78-0 to impeach him, and the Senate decided to proceed with a trial at which Peña was expected to present his defense Friday. Prosecutors also opened three criminal investigations into the collapse of Ueno Bank, including allegations involving Peña and other current and former officials; Peña had not been charged at the observation cutoff.
candidates.title: Paraguay president remains in office pending impeachment trial
